# Balcony garden notes

The balcony faces south-west and receives direct sun from about noon until
sunset. Tomatoes and basil thrive there, but lettuce bolts quickly in July and
should be moved to the shaded side.

Watering happens every morning before eight o'clock. Terracotta pots dry out
faster than plastic ones, so the herbs live in glazed ceramic containers
instead. During a heat wave the schedule changes to twice daily.

Compost comes from a small worm bin kept under the kitchen sink. The worms
prefer vegetable scraps and coffee grounds. Citrus peel and onion skins are
avoided because they slow the bin down.

In October the tomato plants are cut back, the soil is topped up with fresh
compost, and garlic cloves are planted four centimetres deep for the following
summer.
